Class FeederSupport

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.substrate.core.subscription.FeederSupport
public final class FeederSupport extends Object
Shared scaffolding for feeder threads across the three primitives (Atom, Journal, Mailbox). Encapsulates the notifier subscription, semaphore-based wake-up mechanism, thread lifecycle, and exception handling that are identical across all three feeders. Primitive-specific work is supplied via a FeederSupport.FeederStep lambda.

Each primitive's Default*.startFeeder method calls start(String, BiFunction, Handoff, String, FeederSupport.FeederStep) to spawn a feeder virtual thread and returns the canceller closure as the subscription's cleanup hook.

  • Method Details

    • start

      public static Runnable start(String key, BiFunction<String, Consumer<Notification>, NotifierSubscription> subscribeFn, Handoff<?> handoff, String threadName, FeederSupport.FeederStep step)
      Start a feeder virtual thread that drives step in a loop until the step returns false, the thread is interrupted, or a terminal condition fires.

      The feeder subscribes to typed notifications via the provided subscribeFn. On a Notification.Deleted event, the feeder calls handoff.markDeleted() and exits. On any uncaught RuntimeException from the step, the feeder calls handoff.error(cause) and exits. The notifier subscription is always cancelled in a finally block.

      Parameters:
      key - the backend-qualified key this feeder is associated with
      subscribeFn - a subscribe function already bound to the correct primitive type (e.g. notifier::subscribeToAtom)
      handoff - the handoff that the step will push values into; also the target of markDeleted and error when those events fire
      threadName - the virtual thread name prefix (e.g., "substrate-atom-feeder")
      step - the primitive-specific work to run on each iteration
      Returns:
      a canceller closure that, when run, stops the feeder cooperatively — it clears the running flag, wakes the loop, and cancels the notifier subscription. The feeder thread is never interrupted, so a step already blocked in a backend call runs to completion before the loop exits.
